Priya D.: Prepare benchmark script and expected metrics template (due 2026-10-15)
Evan: Provide token distribution sample (p50/p95/p99 lengths) and traffic histogram (due 2026-10-16)

meeting_header: Attendees: Jordan Kim (Redwood AE), Priya Desai (Redwood SE), Evan Martinez (Cerulean Head of ML), Priya Kohli (Cerulean Platform Eng), Samir Patel (CTO), Lila Gomez (Product)
summary: Kickoff scoping call to define a 4-week POC for Cerulean Logistics focused on integrating Redwood's OpenAI-compatible endpoints and SDKs into their route-optimization assistant.

Primary goals: validate latency SLOs for 95th percentile under production-like load, confirm cost per 1M tokens with batching and caching, and prove structured JSON output reliability for downstream systems.
Key risks: VPC/networking constraints for Private deployment, on-prem airgap for certain customers, and dataset privacy requirements (KMS).
Agreement on a 2-day benchmark run with Redwood-managed agents using Cerulean sample workload and 3 golden prompts; security docs to be exchanged prior to bench window.
topics: Workload sizing: RPS, tokens per request, burst patterns
Benchmark design: p50/p95/p99 latency, throughput, token cost
Integration plan: SDK usage, OpenAI-compatible endpoints, function/tool calling, structured output (JSON schema)
Deployment mode options: Hosted API vs Dedicated vs Private VPC
Security and compliance: SOC2, KMS, SSO/SAML, audit logs
transcript: [00:00] Host intro: Jordan: Hey everyone thanks for joining, we have about an hour, quick intros?
[00:05] Evan (Cerulean): Hey, Evan here, head of ML. We want to run a pilot to replace parts of our routing assistant with an LLM for ETA predictions and exception reasoning.
[00:15] Priya D. (Redwood SE): Great, I'm Priya I will land the technical bits. Quick note: we're planning a 4-week POC with a 2-day benchmark window in the middle to validate perf and cost.

[00:30] Samir (CTO): Our main concern is latency at scale. We have spurts of traffic — up to 200 RPS during peak for the assistant. Typical token length is 80 tokens but some ask chains go to 800 tokens.
[00:45] Jordan: Good, that's helpful. For success criteria can we align on p95 under 400ms for short prompts and p95 under 800ms for long prompts?
[01:00] Lila (Product): We need structured output — a JSON schema that includes ETA, confidence score, and a list of suggested follow-ups. Downstream systems expect strict keys.

[01:15] Priya K. (Platform): On networking, we require VPC peering for private pilot; we cannot expose PII to hosted multitenant endpoints unless it's encrypted. We use HashiCorp Vault and AWS KMS for keys.

[01:35] Priya D.: Noted. For POC we can do two tracks: hosted OpenAI-compatible endpoints for fast iteration, and a dedicated VPC connector for a private plane if you want to test with real data. We'll provide docs for KMS integration.

[02:00] Evan: For workloads, p50 token len ~ 60, p95 ~ 320, p99 ~ 760. Our baseline latency with existing microservices for the non-LLM path is ~120ms. We're okay with an incremental 200-300ms on average if it's reliable.

[02:25] Priya D.: Perfect, that gives us targets. We'll design the benchmark to replay your traffic histogram — bursty windows included. Our bench will measure p50/p95/p99 latency, throughput, and token cost per 1M tokens with batching profiles.

[02:45] Jordan: Also will run correctness/quality tests — structured output pass/fail rates with your JSON schema, and a small eval set for hallucination checks. Success criteria: >98% schema compliance, <2% critical hallucinations on golden prompts.
[03:10] Samir: What's the approach for function/tool calling? We use a microservice for routing decisions; ideally the model returns a structured call that our runtime can execute, not free text.

[03:25] Priya D.: Redwood supports function calling and tool invocation patterns. For POC we'll show both: OpenAI-compatible function calls for your microservice stubs, and a structured output mode with explicit JSON. We'll provide sample SDK snippets in Node and Python.
[03:55] Evan: We want to test both the SDK approach and a direct REST OpenAI-compatible endpoint so we can compare latency and ease of integration.

[04:05] Priya D.: Yes. SDKs add convenience but the REST endpoints are the same underneath. Important tradeoffs: SDK can do automatic streaming and retries; REST gives you full control. We'll instrument both in the bench.

[04:30] Jordan: Budget and timeline — proposed 4-week pilot: week 1 onboarding & infra (set up test keys, VPC peering if needed), week 2 integration + small smoke tests, week 3 2-day benchmark + analysis, week 4 iterate on tuning and review.
[04:50] Samir: Budget — what's the expected billing model for the pilot? We need rough numbers to sign off.

[05:00] Jordan: We'll do usage-based for hosted, and a short-term dedicated estimate for dedicated infra during the bench. I will send a line-item estimate for expected token consumption based on your traffic profile.
[05:20] Lila: On success criteria again: schema compliance, latency SLOs, cost per 1M tokens target, and an internal product signoff from PM and Eng.
[05:35] Evan: Also observability — we need per-request traces, token breakdowns, and ability to export logs to our Splunk instance. Audit logs are a must for regulated clients.

[05:50] Priya D.: Redwood Console supports token-level cost breakdowns and tracing hooks. For the POC we'll enable debug-level logging for bench runs and share a dashboard template. Splunk export can be done via syslog or S3 export of logs.
[06:10] Priya K.: Security team will ask for SOC2 report, network diagrams, and key handling notes. Also we need RBAC controls — devs vs prod keys.

[06:25] Jordan: We'll push SOC2/ISO docs and a network diagram in the security pack. Also include SSO options (SAML) and RBAC roles. For KMS, Redwood can integrate with customer-managed keys in the private deployment.
[06:45] Evan: For benchmarks, what models will you test? We'll need to know latencies for both standard and quantized variants.

[06:55] Priya D.: We'll start with two model families: a latency-optimized smaller model for short prompts, and a higher-capacity model for long conversational flows. We'll also test a quantized int8 variant to measure cost reductions. We'll document p95 latency and tokens/sec under batching.
[07:20] Samir: Important: our traffic sometimes requires predictable tail latency. If you use batching to save cost, can you guarantee batching won't blow up p99?

[07:30] Priya D.: Good point. Bench will include configurations: aggressive batching (for cost) and latency-first batching (small batch sizes). We'll collect p99 and show tradeoffs. Redwood's runtime supports per-route batching policies so you can pick per-endpoint SLOs.
[07:50] Lila: Are there any constraints around model version pinning? We need to ensure deterministic behavior during the POC.
[07:58] Jordan: Yes, POC will pin model versions. We'll snapshot model hashes and config. Rollouts can be tested separately once POC proves out.
[08:10] Evan: For structured output validation, can you run automated schema checks during bench and fail noisy responses?

[08:18] Priya D.: Absolutely. We'll run JSON schema validators and compute schema compliance rates. We'll also instrument automatic repair heuristics for minor parse errors to reflect realistic integration.
[08:35] Samir: How about caching? We have repeated similar prompts for ETA calculations when route hasn't changed.
[08:42] Priya D.: Redwood supports prefix and KV cache. For POC we can enable prefix caching for identical prompts and tune TTLs. Bench will capture cache hit rates and cost impact.
[09:00] Evan: What telemetry will you share? We need per-route token counts, latency percentiles, error rates, model fallback events, and cost estimations.
[09:12] Jordan: We'll provide per-route dashboards and a CSV export with those metrics. Also a short post-bench report with recommendations (batch sizes, quantization suggestions, model choices).
[09:30] Priya K.: On the VPC peering track, can you estimate time to set up if our infra team does not have prior Redwood experience?

[09:38] Priya D.: Typical VPC peering and test ingress takes 3-5 business days. We'll provide a runbook and a small template CloudFormation/Terraform snippet to speed it up. For on-prem/air-gapped it's longer and requires an STS session — not recommended for a short POC.
[09:58] Lila: We have a compliance ask: all logs touching PII must be encrypted-at-rest and deleted after 90 days. Can Redwood support retention policies?
[10:08] Jordan: Yes. Redwood has configurable retention windows and can route logs to your S3 with lifecycle policies. We'll document the deletion flow.

[10:25] Evan: Bench specifics: we want two golden prompt sets — route status short prompts (avg 60 tokens) and exception reasoning chains (avg 420 tokens). We'll include 50 evaluation items each for hallucination/accuracy checks.
[10:45] Priya D.: Great. We'll also simulate burst traffic with the histogram you provide. For cost estimate, send us a 7-day sample and we'll model 1M-token buckets for the pilot.
[11:00] Samir: If the pilot succeeds, what's the path to Dedicated or Private?

[11:08] Jordan: Post-pilot we can transition to Redwood Dedicated capacity for predictable throughput; pricing transitions to reserved capacity. For full Private VPC with customer-managed keys there is an enterprise onboarding with additional setup time.
[11:20] Lila: Any blockers you foresee?

[11:25] Priya D.: The main blockers are: getting the sample traffic and VPC permissions in time; also security signoff may delay the bench window if SOC docs requested. If we get artifacts by 2026-10-16 we can keep the proposed schedule.

[11:40] Jordan: Ok quick recap of next steps: Jordan to send SOW and pricing, Priya to prep bench script, Cerulean to send traffic samples and golden prompts, security pack exchange, schedule bench window. Any other asks?
[11:55] Evan: No, that covers it. Looking forward to the bench.
[11:58] Jordan: Thanks everyone we'll follow up with the schedule and docs. Meeting adjourned.
